crimes through the ncrpcfcfrms system most of us know the pain points crypto sellers who unknowingly deal with scammers end up losing twice their crypto is gone and their rupee bank accounts get frozen or lienmarked as proceeds of crime it feels like the system is punishing intermediaries alongside the fraudsters the new sop is trying to change that it lays down guiding principles of proportionality transparency and fairness and introduces grievance redressal timelines and interim custody processes so genuine actors arent left in limbo it explicitly says victims and intermediaries should not face undue hardship para 94 virtual asset service providers is especially relevant for crypto if scammed money has been used to buy cryptocurrency exchanges and wallet providers must freeze those assets once notified they must share basic account and transaction details with authorities the crypto isnt automatically confiscated whether its restored or attached depends on further legal or court processes in plain terms the sop is telling crypto platforms to hold suspicious assets temporarily while courts and investigators decide what happens next thats a big shift from blunt freezes toward a more balanced system that said its still early days theres no clarity yet on how existing account freezes linked to crypto transactions will be treated especially in cases where the underlying usdt or other tokens may already have been transmitted abroad to places like china or cambodia if implemented properly this sop could mean fewer double victims and more clarity for genuine sellers who unknowingly transact with scammers its not perfect yet but its paving the way for a fairer rightsconscious approach to cybercrime recovery as of now the onus is on binance and other platforms to comply let us wait and see what they do
